title: Adding the Tens, Then the Ones

steps.body: Another road: split EVERY addend into tens and ones, add all the tens, add all the ones, then rejoin the two piles.
steps.narration: Another road: split EVERY addend into tens and ones, add all the tens, add all the ones, then rejoin the two piles.

widget.prompt: Tens pile first: 30 + 20 banked 50. Now hop the ones pile of 9... shown as one 9-hop? No — hop by ones is slow. Hop the banked 50 by one ten to preview 60, the neighborhood of the answer.

commonLandings.feedback: That hop is a single one — the preview hop here is a full ten.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop adds 10. From 50, 1 hops land on 60.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 60 — the real answer 59 lives one step below; the tens pile put you in the right neighborhood.

predict.prompt: Split 34 + 25 by place: what are the two piles?
predict.reveal: Tens meet tens and ones meet ones — crossing them mixes unit sizes.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2n by place.
invariants: Regrouping addends changes the ORDER of joining, never the total — every staging of the sum must land on the same number for g2n by place.
misconceptions: Believing the grouping or order of addends can change a sum, or letting an addend join twice or not at all while restaging.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which single change to the staging would actually change the total — and which only changes the path?

explanationVariants: Tens with tens, ones with ones.

widget.prompt: Split 37 + 23 by place before adding. Which split is right?

options.label: 30 + 20 and 7 + 3
options.feedback: Correct — tens meet tens (30 + 20) and ones meet ones (7 + 3); the two little sums rebuild the big one.

options.label: 30 + 3 and 7 + 20
options.feedback: That crosses the places — a ten added to a one mixes two different unit sizes.

options.label: 37 + 20 and 3
options.feedback: 37 was never split, so its ones would be counted inside AND outside the pair.

options.label: 30 + 20 and 7 − 3
options.feedback: The ones join by addition here — nothing in 37 + 23 calls for taking away.

hints: Tens with tens, ones with ones.

widget.prompt: A learner has a tens pile of 50 and a ones pile of 9. Add the ones pile exactly, not as a preview.
widget.missFeedback: One hop of 9 from 50 lands on 59.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — 50 and 9 rebuild the exact total, 59.

widget.prompt: A learner splits 15 + 11 by place. Which statement is true?

options.label: Tens make 20 and ones make 6
options.feedback: Correct — tens meet tens (10 + 10) and ones meet ones (5 + 1); the two little sums rebuild the big one.

options.label: Tens make 6 and ones make 20
options.feedback: That crosses the places — a ten added to a one mixes two different unit sizes.

options.label: Each number keeps only its ones
options.feedback: 15 was never split, so its ones would be counted inside AND outside the pair.

options.label: Place value is not useful here
options.feedback: The ones join by addition here — nothing in 15 + 11 calls for taking away.
